title: paged KV cache: block manager allocator reuse and pinning to reduce allocation churn and eviction races
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Improves paged KV cache block manager: allocator reuse, block pinning, and reduced allocation churn leading to measurable throughput and latency improvements. No breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: The paged KV cache block manager has been a hotspot during high-concurrency streaming workloads due to frequent small allocations, early eviction of blocks that were still in-flight, and fragmentation of the allocator pool. This PR implements a targeted set of improvements: (1) a reusable allocator pool to avoid per-block heap allocations under load, (2) explicit block pinning for in-flight KV pages to prevent accidental eviction races, and (3) an improved reuse/eviction heuristic that prefers reclaimed contiguous ranges and reduces fragmentation.

Summary of changes:
- Add a BlockAllocatorPool that keeps a bounded pool of pre-allocated block chunks and hands out blocks with amortized O(1) allocation cost. The pool is thread-safe and uses a small per-thread cache to avoid contention.
- Introduce Block::pin()/unpin() and a pin_count tracked by the block manager; pinned blocks are excluded from eviction and counted by metrics.
- Modify eviction policy: prefer reclaiming unpinned oldest-last used ranges and coalesce free adjacent blocks before returning memory to the allocator pool.
- Implement fast-path reuse: when a block is freed, it is offered back into the allocator pool instead of returning to the system allocator; repeated allocations of similarly sized pages reuse existing backend memory.
- Add background scavenger that trims the allocator pool under low memory/high pressure conditions (configurable thresholds).
- Add unit and concurrency tests for pinning semantics, allocator reuse, and eviction under race conditions.
- Add a micro-benchmark and integration benchmark showing end-to-end improvements under common continuous-batching workloads.
- Add metrics and traces: kv.block_reuse_rate, kv.allocation_churn_total, kv.pin_evictions_total, kv.allocator_pool_size_gauge, and span annotations for pin/unpin.

Commits summary:
- feat(kv): add BlockAllocatorPool and per-thread caches
- feat(kv): add block pin/unpin and pin-count tracking
- perf(kv): coalesce free ranges and prefer contiguous reuse
- test(kv): add multi-threaded block_manager concurrency tests
- bench(kv): add throughput and latency benchmarks for paged KV cache
- docs: update docs/kv_cache.md with allocator pool tunables and metrics

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/kv/block_allocator.h (+180/-12)
- runtime/kv/block_allocator.cc (+320/-30)
- runtime/kv/paged_block_manager.h (+60/-8)
- runtime/kv/paged_block_manager.cc (+220/-90)
- runtime/kv/paged_kv_cache.cc (+45/-10)
- runtime/kv/tests/block_manager_test.cc (+70/-20)
- benchmarks/kv_cache/throughput_bench.cc (+40/-5)
- docs/kv_cache.md (+20/-3)
- observability/metrics/kv_cache.prom (+15/-0)
- ci/kv_cache_smoke.sh (+10/-0)
- third_party/allocators/README (+12/-20)

Small illustrative snippets:
- block_allocator.h: added GetReusableBlock() and ReturnBlockToPool(Block*) APIs; BlockAllocatorPool constructor exposes max_pool_entries tunable.
- paged_block_manager.cc: before eviction we now check block->pin_count.load() == 0 and skip pinned blocks; coalesceFreeRanges() runs inline to reduce churn.

Benchmarks & results:
- Throughput (tokens/sec) on dedicated GPU pool, mixed prompt lengths, batch_size=32: baseline: 54k TPS -> this branch: 59k TPS (+9.3%).
- Tail latency (p99) under continuous batching: baseline: 280ms -> this branch: 246ms (-12.1%).
- System-level allocations: malloc/realloc syscalls measured dropped ~42% in a synthetic alloc-heavy trace.
- Memory churn metric kv.allocation_churn_total decreased by ~35% in the bench harness.

Testing and CI:
- CI run: build -> unit tests -> integration smoke -> bench smoke. Initial CI run reported a flaky test in block_manager_test (race on unpin path) which was fixed by adding stronger ordering in the pin/unpin atomic sequence and a targeted unit test. Final CI: all checks passed. Bench CI (non-gating) shows the throughput numbers above in the attached artifacts.

Review conversation (high level):
- Maya Singh: "Can you clarify the invariants around pin/unpin when eviction and scavenger run concurrently? Also please add a metric for pinned_block_count."
- Author (Ava): "Added doc comments in paged_block_manager.h and exposed kv.pinned_blocks_gauge; updated tests to cover concurrent scavenger + pin scenarios."
- Carlos Rivera: "The per-thread cache may grow unbounded in pathological workloads. Can we cap it and add a debug-only assertion?"
- Author: "Cap added (configurable per-thread cache size), and a debug-only ASSERT that triggers if we ever exceed twice the configured cap."
- Noah Brooks: "Bench numbers look promising. Please add a small experiment to validate under high-multiplexing small prompts."
- Author: "Added an extra bench config and included results in the PR description."
- Reviewers approved after fixes; marked for merge.

Risk and rollout plan:
- This change is behind a runtime flag (kv.paged_block_manager_v2=on) and disabled by default for customers. We plan a staged rollout: internal dogfood -> canary infra -> general availability. The allocator pool has configurable size and scavenger thresholds to tune for different memory footprints.

Operational notes:
- New metrics allow SRE to track allocation churn and pinned block evictions. Added dashboards: Observability -> KV Cache -> Block Manager (new panel).
- If customers experience unexpected memory growth, lowering kv.allocator_pool_max_entries or enabling scavenger_aggressiveness should remediate.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after CI passed and reviewers approved. Backported a small fix to the release/2026-02 branch in a follow-up hotfix PR for an internal dogfood cluster that hit an allocator edge-case.
